children: BioNTech said it decided to terminate a midstage clinical trial of a potential treatment for colorectal cancer.

The decision follows a new recommendation from the independent Data Safety Monitoring Board, which in its most recent review of data from the trial identified a numerical imbalance in overall survival between treatment arms in the patient population, BioNTech said Friday.
DSMB told BioNTech that continuing the trial was unlikely to change the efficacy outcome, and the organization recommended discontinuing treatment of patients and terminating the trial.
Shares of BioNTech fell 8.2%, to $102.22. Despite the loss, shares are up 5.7% year to date.
The Phase 2 clinical trial was evaluating autogene cevumeran, an investigational individualized mRNA cancer immunotherapy, and its ability to treat certain colorectal cancers.
The treatment is being jointly developed by BioNTech and Genentech. BioNTech said it made the decision to terminate the trial in consultation with Genentech.
"Any decision concerning clinical trials is made with utmost care, keeping patients as our highest priority," said Ozlem Tureci, cofounder and chief medical officer at BioNTech.

"While this outcome is not what we had envisioned for mRNA as a monotherapy in colorectal cancer, it provides scientific insight into the challenges of treating immunotherapy-insensitive tumor types with immune-suppressive microenvironments and will help inform the further development of investigational mRNA cancer immunotherapies."
